P1-23.P1_flat: - Access command fields. For accesses on a record port (never on non-record ports, even ones together carrying an access) addressing this unit's own registers, FIFOs, locks or memory words (not a cache's copies), the fields only saying whether an access happens, its direction and which register, FIFO or bytes it reaches (a strobe, a read or write bit, register-select address bits, byte enables; an address indexing a memory's stored words is the access address, not one of them), and a write enable whose assignment reads only these fields and that only lets a register or FIFO take the written data, are part of the information the access writes or reads, not information of their own. They are not pieces of their own, although steps 1 and 2, Build-time values and Per-region checks would keep some: keep no concept for them; cite no line only testing them, or only assigning such a write enable, as a held line. A signal of its own decoded from these fields that gates or masks what a read returns (a read enable, a select also masking read data), or pops a FIFO of data the unit generates itself, is its own piece (step 2): name it by what it decides and hold it at the line assigning it; no step-3 clause folds it. An inline condition is no such signal, nor is a strobe of a FIFO that Port buffers covers. Such a field whose value a register takes as its new content belongs to that register's piece. Not covered: a request held until served, a select routing it on, and a strobe driven on to a unit output port other than as an acknowledge; an operation's start pulse (not an access's strobe or write enable).

  Criteria (any of): (1) the fields only saying whether an access happens, its direction and which register, FIFO or bytes it reaches (a strobe, a read or write bit, register-select address bits, byte enables; an address indexing a memory's stored words is the access address, not one of them); (2) a write enable whose assignment reads only these fields and that only lets a register or FIFO take the written data.
  Exceptions: Not covered: a request held until served, a select routing it on, and a strobe driven on to a unit output port other than as an acknowledge; an operation's start pulse (not an access's strobe or write enable).
  Outcome: they are part of the information the access writes or reads, not information of their own; such a field whose value a register takes as its new content belongs to that register's piece. They are not pieces of their own, although steps 1 and 2, Build-time values and Per-region checks would keep some: keep no concept for them.
  Evidence: cite no line only testing them, or only assigning such a write enable, as a held line.
- Access command fields (b).
  Scope: A signal of its own decoded from these fields.
  Criteria (any of): (1) gates or masks what a read returns (a read enable, a select also masking read data); (2) pops a FIFO of data the unit generates itself.

P1-23.P2_flat: For accesses on a record port (never on non-record ports, even ones together carrying an access) addressing this unit's own registers, FIFOs, locks or memory words (not a cache's copies), the fields only saying whether an access happens, its direction and which register, FIFO or bytes it reaches (a strobe, a read or write bit, register-select address bits, byte enables; an address indexing a memory's stored words is the access address, not one of them), and a write enable whose assignment reads only these fields and that only lets a register or FIFO take the written data, are part of the information the access writes or reads, not information of their own. They never qualify for any conceptual asset, whether or not the port is a bus request or response record, and can be secondaries (2.7, direction b) of the element the access writes, reads or decides. Judged as usual: a separate signal decoded from these fields that gates or masks what a read returns or pops a FIFO of data the unit generates itself (the decision's own element), a register loaded with such a field's value, a request held until served, a select routing it on, a strobe driven on to a unit output port other than as an acknowledge, and an operation's start pulse (not an access's strobe or write enable).

P1-22.P1_flat: - Operation selectors. In a unit executing an instruction or atomic memory operation a processor issues to it (a coprocessor, an atomic read-modify-write), instruction or request fields only picking the operation or the result form returned (an opcode, a function code, an instruction-type bit), their stored copies, and flags decoded from them only naming the operation are part of that operation (step 3), not pieces of their own, although step 2 names a select. Do not list them under "Enters Through" or cite their lines as held lines, except a line assigning an element this rule judges as usual. Judged as usual: a start command or pulse saying when the operation starts, even one decoded per operation (a multiply or divide start), a register access's address and write enable, a completion flag, and a setting decoded from them that changes how operands are read (signedness). A plain bus read or write, its read or write bit and a read enable made from it are not covered. In a unit executing an instruction or atomic memory operation a processor issues to it, a register whose value, apart from constants and itself, comes only from one source operand input (a port or a request-record field, not of a bus request (2.6)) when the operation starts, directly or through its next-value wire, and reaches an output port only through the element holding the result, only holds that operand while the operation uses it (2.6: a copy kept only while the value moves). It and its next-value wire are part of that operand's piece: keep that piece, list the operand input under "Enters Through", cite the lines where it takes the operand as entry lines, and do not cite them as held lines.

P1-27.P1_flat: - Processor context fields. A field, of a record input port other than a bus request or response record port (2.6), that tells the processor's privilege mode, whether it is in debug mode or takes a trap, or whether the current access is a fetch or data access, read or write, only refines a decision this unit computes from other information when this unit reads it and only tests it (a condition, select, compare with a fixed value, gate on another result), directly or through a wire only selecting between such fields: the processor holds that state; the record carries a copy. Such a field or wire is part of the decision it refines (step 3), not a piece of its own, although steps 1 and 2 would name it and 2.4, 4.2 and 4.4 point at privilege and debug modes: keep no concept for it, nor list it under "Enters Through" or cite its lines as held lines, except a line assigning an element this rule judges as usual. Judged as usual: the decision such a field refines, where computed or stored (a permission verdict, fault output, execution state); the access address, compared with stored state; and the address, write enable and data of a write to a register of this unit. Not covered: the whole record port, a non-record input port (a peer's flow-control line, an interrupt or debug request), and a port or field wired into an instance. Judge what a field tells from port field names and their uses; say so.
